title: TruckScenes LiDAR detector feasibility: CenterPoint no-go (spconv has no Windows wheel), PointPillars verified runnable zero-shot on CPU
dataset: MAN TruckScenes v1.2-mini (one LIDAR_TOP_FRONT sample, scene index 0)
sensor_configuration: LiDAR only, single channel, single sample -- feasibility check, not a scored run

environment.hardware: AMD Ryzen 7 5700U with Radeon Graphics -- no NVIDIA GPU, CPU-only
environment.python: 3.11.9, truckscenes-devkit/detection-env (same venv as EXP-0006/0010/0016, reused as-is)

commands: pip install spconv   # FAILED on this machine -- see notes
python pointpillars_minimal_test.py  # loads model, loads one real TruckScenes LIDAR_TOP_FRONT sample, pads to 5 point-features, runs inference_detector, unpacks tuple result

measurements.name: centerpoint_spconv_install_result
measurements.scope: pip install spconv (CPU package) on this Windows machine: fails, 0 compatible wheels found. PyPI metadata for spconv==2.3.8 lists only manylinux2014_x86_64 wheels for Python 3.9-3.13 -- no Windows wheel exists for the CPU package

measurements.name: pointpillars_checkpoint_size_bytes
measurements.scope: downloaded nuScenes-pretrained PointPillars checkpoint file size

measurements.name: pointpillars_minimal_execution_raw_boxes
measurements.scope: raw predicted boxes (before score threshold) from one real TruckScenes LIDAR_TOP_FRONT sample, 17,180 points, zero-shot CPU inference

measurements.name: pointpillars_minimal_execution_boxes_above_threshold
measurements.scope: same single-sample run, boxes with score >= 0.10 (same threshold used throughout EXP-0006/0010/0016)

notes: AD-S3-1 bullet 2, LiDAR half. CenterPoint (the candidate informally flagged since EXP-0006) is a documented no-go on this machine: its SparseEncoder middle layer needs spconv, and spconv's CPU-labelled PyPI package ships no Windows wheel at all (verified against PyPI release metadata, not assumed) -- distinct from and more specific than the earlier 'no NVIDIA GPU' framing, since even the non-CUDA build can't be installed here. PointPillars (same nuScenes pretrained-checkpoint family, no spconv dependency -- confirmed by grepping every PointPillars base config for SparseEncoder/spconv, zero matches) was checked instead: code, checkpoint (SHA-256 verified), and licence (Apache-2.0, same as mmdet3d itself) all check out; class mapping reuses the existing NUSC_TO_TRUCKSCENES table from the FCOS3D work unchanged. Two small preprocessing fixes were needed and verified empirically, not assumed: (1) TruckScenes' own devkit returns 4-feature points (x,y,z,intensity) but the nuScenes loading pipeline needs a 5th zeroed sweep-time column, caught via a real IndexError on first attempt; (2) inference_detector returns a (result, data) tuple, not a bare result. With both fixes applied, a real minimal execution on one true TruckScenes LiDAR sample completed in seconds on CPU: 41 raw boxes, 11 above the 0.10 score threshold. This is deliberately not a scored result (one sample, no ground truth compared) -- it establishes only that the candidate is runnable end-to-end on this hardware. Per docs/dataset-suitability.md, this does not reopen D-04 (already answered on TruckDrive) or the recorded-radar-range limitation on TruckScenes; it is scoped to whether a second modality is runnable on TruckScenes at all, for a defensible camera-vs-LiDAR comparison on one dataset.
